rules.description: Summaries and adaptations must preserve the factual meaning of verified facts.
Uses must remain within the package's allowed framing and avoid prohibited framing.
Every disclosure relevant to a use must be communicated to the reader.
Details may be omitted unless the omission would materially change a reasonable reader's interpretation.
Developing, disputed, alleged, estimated, uncertain, or unverified information must not be stated as established.
Direct quotations and their attribution must remain exact; paraphrases must not be presented as quotes.
Changing format does not relax factual, contextual, framing, disclosure, attribution, quote, or confidence rules.
Do not add facts unsupported by the editorial package.
Do not create quotations absent from the editorial package.
Do not alter verified quotation text while presenting it as direct speech.
Do not use any framing explicitly prohibited by the package.
Do not omit material context in a way that changes the reporting's meaning.
Do not represent information with greater certainty than the package supports.
